name: [medium][work-software] ecommerce-microservices-architecture-discussion

conversation.content: Hey, can we review the high-level architecture I drafted for the new e-commerce platform? I’m thinking microservices with an event-driven backbone.
Sure. What’s your tech stack preference? I’ve seen a lot of teams go with Node.js for services these days.
Yeah, Node.js with TypeScript. I strongly prefer functional programming over OOP, so we’ll use patterns like currying and composition. No classes if we can avoid it.
Makes sense. And for databases? I’d recommend PostgreSQL for relational data and Redis for caching. Also, with microservices you’ll need a message broker for async communication.
Exactly. We’re using Kafka for event streaming. That’ll handle order events, payment confirmations, stock updates. I already set up a local test cluster yesterday.
Good. What about containerization? Docker and Kubernetes are pretty standard for deployment.

Yes, Docker for each service, and we’ll run on a small Kubernetes cluster. We’re planning to deploy to EKS once the MVP is ready. By the way, the user service migration to the new auth system was completed last week. That’s a big milestone.
Nice! So user service is already on the new stack. What about team processes? Do you have a fixed schedule for stand-ups and code reviews?
Yeah, we do daily stand-ups at 9:30 AM sharp. Code reviews are mandatory via GitHub pull requests. No direct pushes to main. That keeps quality high.
Smart. How about tooling for local development? Are you using any particular editor or package manager preference?
I’m all in on VS Code with Prettier and ESLint. And I prefer Yarn over npm – it’s faster and the lockfile is more reliable. We enforce that across the team with a `.yarnrc`.
Solid choices. Now about the memory leak in the order service – how was that resolved? I saw it mentioned in the bug tracker.

Ah, that was a pain. Turned out we weren’t closing database connections properly in some handlers. Once we added a `finally` block to release connections, the leak stopped. It was actually in the order creation endpoint.
Good fix. So what’s the next milestone? We should plan the deployment pipeline after the order service refactor.
Right, after the refactor we’ll set up CI/CD with GitHub Actions. Then deploy the user and product services to staging on Kubernetes. I’ll share the architecture diagram tomorrow.
Looking forward to it. Let me know if you need help with Kafka configurations or Kubernetes manifests.

golden_facts: Tech stack: Node.js with TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Redis, Docker, Kubernetes, Kafka for event streaming.
User prefers functional programming patterns and avoids class-based OOP.
User service migration to new auth system completed last week.
Daily stand-ups at 9:30 AM. Code reviews mandatory via GitHub pull requests.
User uses VS Code with Prettier and ESLint, prefers Yarn over npm.
Memory leak in order service was caused by unclosed database connections; fixed by adding a finally block.
